$comment: Single source of truth for the theme. scripts/build-tokens.js generates scss/_tokens.scss and the :root blocks in css/cambridge-tokens.css from this file — edit here, then `npm run build`. A token with a "dark" value is re-declared for dark mode in the CSS build (the Bootstrap build has no dark mode yet, so _tokens.scss only ever sees "value").

ink.comment: Pantone 547. The dominant structural colour: body text, headings, primary buttons, nav text. Not an accent — this is the colour the page is built from. In dark mode it flips to a pale tint, because what it names is 'the text and primary-control colour', not 'the navy'; the navy fill lives on as --cam-deep and the surfaces.

inkDeep.comment: Hover/active shade of ink (primary button hover). Darker than ink in light mode, brighter in dark mode — 'further from the page'.

onInk.comment: Text or icon colour sitting on an --cam-ink fill: the primary button, the checked checkbox's tick.

muted.comment: Secondary text. Darkened from a first pass (#5b7480) to clear WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both --bg and --surface.

surface.comment: Card/panel background. Lighter than --bg in dark mode too (elevation reads as lighter, not darker).

fill.comment: Subtle fill for inputs, chips, quiet notices.

accent.comment: The light blue from the Centre's logo (assets/cms-mark.svg). The one accent colour — used at low density: a header rule, an active nav underline, a notice edge. On a light page it is never a text or background fill by itself (2.4:1 on white, 2.4:1 white on it — fails AA both directions). On a dark page it would clear AA as text (6.4:1 on --surface) but is kept to the same thin uses so the two modes read alike.

accentInk.comment: Accent at text-level contrast, for hover text and anything accent-coloured that has to be read. Darkened logo blue in light mode (6.8:1 on --bg, 6.4:1 on --fill); a lighter tint of it in dark mode (8.6:1 on --surface).

deep.comment: Fill for the full-bleed deep hero band (.cam-hero-deep), white text on it. The same navy as --ink in light mode; a separate token because --ink flips to a pale tint in dark mode. Lifted slightly in dark mode so the band stays distinguishable from --surface.

danger.comment: Red Ribbon. Errors only. Unchanged in dark mode: as a badge fill it must keep holding white text (5.3:1), which a lighter red would not.

focus.comment: Focus ring colour — same as ink.

overlay.comment: The tint over a page behind a modal. Ink (19 56 68) at low alpha rather than neutral black, so the page dims into the same family as everything else here. Dark mode needs a much heavier veil: a 24% tint barely moves a page that is already dark.

overlayBlur.comment: Blur radius behind a modal. Enough that body text stops being readable — the page should read as out of focus, not merely tinted — while its shapes stay recognisable enough to place the box in context.

shadowModal.comment: The only elevation in the theme, for a modal. Ink-deep (12 38 46) rather than black, which reads grey against these blue-greens. Two layers: a wide soft one for the lift, a tight one to seat the edge. In dark mode a tinted shadow is invisible, so it is plain black at higher alpha.

chartAnon.comment: Science Blue. Categorical data series 1. Dark mode lifts all three series to clear 3:1 against --surface.

fontSans.comment: Cambridge's specified secondary face. Body text, UI chrome.

fontSerif.comment: Stand-in for Feijoa (Klim Type Foundry, no free web-embeddable licence). Headings and the wordmark only.

gutter.comment: The one horizontal breathing space between page content and the viewport edge. Every .cam-*-inner and .cam-container uses it, so header, hero, body and footer line up at every width.

widthPage.comment: Full-width band content: header, masthead, footer.

widthWide.comment: Wide content column: hero, dashboards, tables.

widthText.comment: Reading measure: prose, forms, narrow pages.

aliases.$comment: Deprecated names, kept so downstream sites that reference the old --cam-teal / $cam-teal don't silently lose their accent when it changed from teal to the logo blue. Each maps old token name -> new token name. In CSS the alias is a var() reference, so it follows the new token into dark mode. Remove once nothing consumes them.

categoricalPalette.comment: The full six-colour Cambridge primary palette, for when you need more than three categories (e.g. a legend with 4-6 series). Not used by the base theme's own components.
